subject: errors
text: - `hook` never writes to stderr and never exits non-zero (Hook Contract). A security check failing in `hook` (server verification mismatch, oversized stdin, strict-modes failure) still ends in exit 0 with no body, so the dialog renders for the human. As landed, `viola hook <event>` runs the stdin cap, the `VIOLA_NAME` / `VIOLA_DIR` shape checks and the one-object parse and, on Linux and Windows, the server verification (macOS the recorded gap), and fails open with `hook-decision` detail `oversize-stdin` · `malformed-json` · `channel-unreachable` · `server-verify-failed`. Before it reads the diagnostics level or initialises obs, the event and dialog paths run the instance's strict-modes check (`canonical`, then `trusted`): a refused or absent instance, a `VIOLA_DIR` naming no existing directory included, exits 0 at once with no `config.json` read, no role file, no stdin read, no line, no frame and no SessionEnd append; the two `--capture` arms run ahead of that check. Its hidden `--capture <DIR>` arm runs the stdin cap, the absolute, existing `<DIR>` check and the exclusive `create_private_new` claim, and writes the capture raw; with `--answers <DIR>` it also runs the `take(64)` closed-`ProbeAnswer` read and `probe_body`'s payload shape check, and prints one `decision_body` body to stdout only for a mapped answer. Its statusline form `hook statusline --capture <DIR> [--shell <WORD>]` runs the same stdin cap and `<DIR>` check and claim, writes the payload raw and the closed shell verdict, and prints nothing on any path. On every failure it prints nothing, its stderr is always empty, and it exits 0 (Decisions Log `2026-09-28`, capture arm; the founder's live ruling of 2026-10-05 on `--answers`; the founder's own answer to P4 fork 3 of chunk 2026-10-13-owed-ledger-rows («Run B + --settings», relayed verbatim by the operator, that chunk's `inputs#I1`), on the statusline form).

subject: errors
text: - A `viola hook` event or dialog whose server check fails writes no frame and exits 0 with empty streams; its `hook-decision` line carries `server-verify-failed` (on the dialog path after `hook-invoked{corr:null}`, with `decision_emitted:false`), and a SessionEnd whose check fails is appended through the direct `append_session_end`.

subject: errors
text: - A `viola hook` event or dialog whose instance snapshot is replayed or absent at `connect` (`read_snapshot_or_replay`; a replayed snapshot carries no `endpoint`, `pid` or `started_at`) writes no frame and fails open as `channel-unreachable`, and a SessionEnd so refused is appended through the direct `append_session_end`.

subject: errors
text: - `viola hook statusline` (without `--capture`) over a replayed snapshot (`read_snapshot_or_replay`) finds no `statusline_command`, so nothing runs and nothing prints; it exits 0 with empty stderr.

subject: errors
text: - A `viola mcp` frame tool (`send` · `wait` · `last` · `answer`) whose server check fails (the connected peer is not the recorded wrapper, or the check cannot be made) sends no frame and returns the result of an unreachable instance: `isError` `instance-unreachable` with `detail` `server-verify-failed`, text `refused: instance-unreachable`; its `error` is `instance-unreachable` as for every cause, and it writes no log line.

subject: errors
text: - A `viola mcp` frame tool runs the instance's strict-modes check (`check_instance`) before its liveness pre-check; a refused check, like a snapshot that is replayed or absent (no live endpoint), sends no frame and returns the unreachable result: `isError` `instance-unreachable`, text `refused: instance-unreachable`, and no log line, `detail` reading `strict-modes-failed` for a refused check and, with no live endpoint, `viola_state::liveness::without_endpoint`'s cause: `instance-dead` for an instance directory, `unwrapped-name` for anything else.

subject: errors
text: - The wrapper's `link` / `unlink` methods answer a failed `record` / `remove` as `-32603` with the fixed message `internal error` and `data: null`. At `viola link` / `viola unlink`, a wrapper error reply (a `-32602` included) is a wrapper fault, exit 20, and a `Refused` reply or an `ok` of a shape other than the verb's own (`link`: a string `since` and a boolean `already_linked`; `unlink`: an object) is an internal error, exit 1.

subject: errors
text: - `viola_channel::sanitised_fault(&Value) -> Option<Value>` is the fault reader of its two callers, `reply_of` (`src/cmd/client.rs`) and `of_reply` (`crates/viola-mcp/src/result.rs`): `None` without an integer `code`; for each of the five known codes `message` is the fault's fixed text and `data` null, save the two `-32602` bodies that keep `data`.

subject: errors
text: - A `-32602` read by `sanitised_fault` keeps `data` in two bodies only: the unsupported-version body, an integer `data.supported` with a `data.wrapper` of 1 to 64 ASCII letters, digits, `.`, `-` or `+`, and the body whose `data.reason` is exactly `release-from-driver`. Any other `-32602` reads `invalid params` with `data` null.

subject: errors
text: - A fault code outside the five reads `{"code": <code>, "message": "wrapper fault", "data": null}`, `wrapper fault` a fixed output word on `--json` and MCP; the human line reads `error: wrapper fault  <code>` (`src/human/mirror.rs`).

subject: errors
text: - `viola_core::is_code_word` admits 1 to 64 bytes of `[a-z0-9-]`, a lower-case letter first. In `reply_of` and `of_reply`, a `refusal` failing it reads `unknown`, a string `detail` failing it reads null, and a non-string `detail` is no known reply.

subject: errors
text: - Exception by design: a code word outside the closed list stays visible in the document and in `refused: <word>`, and its exit is `unknown`'s 14 by `reason_of`.

text: - `ProtocolError::cause` gives `unsupported-version`, `invalid-params` and `release-from-driver` for the three `-32602` faults and nothing for the other four; `ResponseLine`'s `Drop` writes it as `channel-response`'s `detail`, a closed enum (`schemas/diag-line.v1.json`), on both the server's and the client's line.

text: - Absence: no `-32603` is driven in a scanned home, and no failpoint or counted panic drives one there; the unit layer holds it (`answer_a_panicking_dispatch_is_internal_error_and_closes`, `links_set_method_an_append_that_fails_is_internal_with_the_set_unchanged`).

text: - CLI `send` · `wait` · `last` · `answer` · `pause` · `release`, as `link` / `unlink`, run the instance's strict-modes check (`client::refuse_untrusted`: `check_instance` on the home and `instances/<name>`) before any frame: a refusal exits 21, prints the instance pair (`human::instance_state_pair`) through `human::refuse`, or under `--json` exactly `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"strict-modes-failed"}`, opens nothing under the home and writes no line.

subject: errors
text: - Exit 21's `detail` is a closed set of five causes, `strict-modes-failed` · `instance-dead` · `unwrapped-name` · `endpoint-lost` · `server-verify-failed`: the CLI's `--json` document reads `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"<cause>"}`, and MCP's `isError` result the same less `v`, its text `refused: instance-unreachable`.

subject: errors
text: - `viola_core::UnreachableCause` has no serde path; every cause word is written by the two clients: `client::unreachable_document` is the one writer of the CLI's exit-21 document (`refuse_untrusted` and `src/cmd/plugin.rs` through it; `src/cmd/list.rs`'s `refused_document` builds the board's `strict-modes-failed` as a `Value` for `board_document`), and `unreachable` in `crates/viola-mcp/src/result.rs` is MCP's.

subject: errors
text: - The `unwrapped-name` and `endpoint-lost` hints come last on stderr in plain ASCII, their `<name>` the parsed `ViolaName`.

subject: errors
text: - Exception: the exit-2 paths of `viola answer` and `viola send` write the fixed `UNUSABLE_RESPONSE` / `UNUSABLE_TEXT` line to stderr whatever `--json` says, and no document (`src/cmd/answer.rs`, `src/cmd/send.rs`); `NOT_ERROR_BODIES` names them.

subject: errors
text: - `viola run` and `viola revive`'s start run the home tree's strict-modes check (`check_home_tree`, over the instance and the pinned copy's key) before the wrapper log opens: a refusal exits 1 with the home pair for a home-level refusal or the instance pair for an instance-level one, and opens no log, writes no line and starts no child (`revive --json` prints `strict-modes-failed`). `viola verify` runs the check on the home, `ledger/`, `bin/` and `plugin/` before its `cli` log, and a refusal there exits 1 with the home pair, no step line, no summary and no line; `update_stamps`'s `StampsError::StrictModes` exits 1 with the home pair, no step line and no summary, and its `process-exit`, under a parsed `VIOLA_NAME`, carries `strict-modes-failed`. On Unix a home under a regular file (unstattable) is such a refusal (the frame verbs: exit 21, the instance pair); on Windows that path stats `NotFound` and the `cli` catch-site line stands.

text: - Where the `cli` catch site prints its internal-error line (`prints_internal_error`) and `json_asked` (`src/main.rs`) reads `--json` among the arguments before a `--`, `{"v":1,"error":"internal-error","detail":null}` prints on stdout in place of `error: internal error`, stderr empty; `run`, `revive`'s start, `mcp` and `hook` stay silent there.

text: - `collision_check` prints and logs `stale-heartbeat` for a stale holder and `already-live` for a live holder and a fresh replayed beat; a frame verb against a stale instance reads `instance-dead` (`live_endpoint` gives none for a stale wrapper), stale heartbeat being exit 1's cause alone.
